title: Design System: KRW FI / Rates Portfolio Management System

display.purpose: Hero KPI numbers and PriceDisplay big-figure span only.

body-strong.purpose: Table cell emphasis, button labels, active nav item.

label.purpose: Category tags, filter chip labels, column headers — always uppercase, wide tracking.

micro.purpose: Timestamps, footnotes, percentage markers, input suffixes.

shadows.name: sm
shadows.purpose: Dark-mode popovers, dropdowns, floating/dragged dockview panels.

motion.name: color-swap
motion.purpose: Default hover/focus transition for buttons, inputs, nav items — quick, no easing flourish.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single blue submit action per screen — Run Backtest, Add to Sandbox, Run Optimization.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 32px; padding: 0 16px; border-radius: 4px; border: none; background: #3B82F6; color: #FFFFFF; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.5; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.15s ease-out; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #2f6fd1; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px #3B82F6; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.4; pointer-events: none; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Transparent, subtle-bordered action — used beside a primary button or standalone for lower-emphasis actions.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 32px; padding: 0 16px; border-radius: 4px; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.06); background: transparent; color: #FFFFFF; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.5; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.15s ease-out; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: #1A2028; } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px #3B82F6; }

components.name: Filter Chip
components.description: Three-part composite chip used in Portfolio Management's filter bar: uppercase label segment, mixed-case value segment, optional remove icon.
components.html: BOOKCMA RP
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; height: 28px; border-radius: 4px; background: #1A2028; overflow: hidden; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; } .ds-chip-label { display: flex; align-items: center; height: 100%; padding: 0 8px; background: #2A323D; color: #6B7280; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-chip-value { padding: 0 8px; color: #FFFFFF; font-size: 14px; } .ds-chip-remove { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 100%; padding: 0 8px; background: transparent; border: none; color: #4B5563; cursor: pointer; } .ds-chip-remove:hover { color: #A8B0BC; }

components.name: Soft Badge
components.description: Asset-class / status badge used in tables (Top Movers, Positions Grid). Soft background, colored text — never a solid fill except on row hover.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; border-radius: 4px; padding: 4px 8px; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-badge-info { background: rgba(59,130,246,0.14); color: #3B82F6; } .ds-badge-positive { background: rgba(0,193,118,0.14); color: #00C176; } .ds-badge-negative { background: rgba(255,74,92,0.14); color: #FF4A5C; } .ds-badge-risk { background: rgba(245,166,35,0.14); color: #F5A623; }

components.name: Input Field
components.description: Filled text/number input — used across forms (Simulation trade entry, Optimal Portfolio constraints).
components.css: .ds-input-wrap { position: relative; display: flex; align-items: center; } .ds-input { height: 32px; width: 100%; border-radius: 4px; border: 1px solid transparent; background: #2A323D; padding: 0 12px; padding-right: 48px; color: #FFFFFF; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; outline: none; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #4B5563; } .ds-input:focus { border-color: #3B82F6; } .ds-input-suffix { position: absolute; right: 12px; pointer-events: none; color: #6B7280; font-size: 11px; }

components.name: Price Display (Big Figure)
components.description: Signature component. Renders a rate/price in three visual weights — dim base, bold big-figure, dim unit — right-aligned and tabular so consecutive rows align on the big figure. Example: 3.4|567|%.
components.css: .ds-price { display: inline-flex; align-items: baseline; justify-content: flex-end; white-space: nowrap; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-price-base { color: #4B5563; font-size: 14px; } .ds-price-big { color: #FFFFFF; font-weight: 700; font-size: 20px; } .ds-price-unit { color: #4B5563; font-size: 14px; }

components.name: Status Dot (Live)
components.description: 8px status indicator with a pulsing ring when live — used in the top bar's market-data connection status and desk-wide live indicators.
components.css: .ds-status-dot { position: relative; display: inline-flex; height: 8px; width: 8px; } .ds-status-dot-ping { position: absolute; display: inline-flex; height: 100%; width: 100%; border-radius: 9999px; background: #00C176; opacity: 0.6; animation: ds-ping 1.6s cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1) infinite; } .ds-status-dot-core { position: relative; display: inline-flex; height: 8px; width: 8px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #00C176; } @keyframes ds-ping { 75%, 100% { transform: scale(2); opacity: 0; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-status-dot-ping { animation: none; opacity: 0.35; } }

components.name: Sidebar Nav Item
components.description: Sidebar navigation item with the 2px active-state accent bar — the one sanctioned exception to the no-border-stripe rule.
components.html: Home
components.css: .ds-nav-item { position: relative; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; height: 36px; padding: 0 12px; border-radius: 4px; color: #A8B0BC; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; text-decoration: none; } .ds-nav-item:hover { background: #1A2028; } .ds-nav-item-active { background: #1A2028; color: #FFFFFF; } .ds-nav-item-active::before { content: ''; position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; height: 100%; width: 2px; background: #3B82F6; }

narrative.overview: This system speaks the same visual language as Goldman Sachs Marquee — not a clone, a dialect. It sits deliberately between two failure modes: Bloomberg's extreme density, where hierarchy collapses under its own information load, and Robinhood's extreme minimalism, which throws away the density this desk actually needs. The dialect's grammar is information density with breathing room: every pixel earns its place, and the room to breathe comes from luminance steps and typographic weight, never from empty decoration. Two structural doctrines carry the whole system. First, contrast-driven hierarchy — structure is built from 2–5% luminance steps between background layers and from type weight, never from hue. Second, semantic color minimalism — color is reserved for meaning (direction, state, status) and appears only as points: dots, badges, thin lines, emphasized digits. It is never a fill. This system explicitly rejects: any card that 'looks designed' (gradient, shadow, thick border, rounded-lg), decorative panel-background color used 'for visual interest,' gradient text, glassmorphism as a default treatment, numbers in a proportional font, and color used as the primary signal for hierarchy or meaning. Dark and light are not one palette inverted — dark is the trading/monitoring surface, light is the analysis/reporting surface, and each has its own deliberately tuned neutral and semantic ramp.
keyCharacteristics: Backgrounds separated by luminance steps, never by borders
Semantic color (green/red/amber/blue) used only as a meaningful point, never a fill
Tabular, monospace numerics everywhere a number appears
Big-figure notation (3-digit) for every rate and price display
Dark = trading surface, Light = analysis surface — two tuned palettes, not an inversion

rules.name: The Points-Not-Fills Rule
rules.body: Semantic color renders as a dot, badge, thin line, or emphasized digit. The moment a semantic color becomes a panel or card background, it has become decoration — revert it.

rules.name: The Two-Palette Rule
rules.body: Dark and light are not filter: invert() of each other. Each mode's neutral ramp and semantic ramp is independently tuned because they serve two different desk activities.

rules.name: The Case Invariant Rule
rules.body: Category tags are always uppercase with wide tracking; values are always mixed case. There is no exception.

rules.name: The Tabular-Everywhere Rule
rules.body: Any element that renders a number is tabular-nums and, for anything beyond an inline count, JetBrains Mono.

rules.name: The Flat-Panel Rule
rules.body: Cards and panels never receive a shadow at rest. Shadow appears only on transient/overlay surfaces.

rules.name: The Jade/Berry Reservation Rule
rules.body: Jade (positive) and Berry (negative) replace green/red as the P&L semantic pair in all charts; the Jade and Berry hue families are reserved for P&L semantics and never appear as sector colors. Default steps are -80; solid Jade/Berry only for bold elements.

rules.name: The Cool-Family Sector Rule
rules.body: Sector encodings use only Blue/Navy/Aqua hues, differentiated by luminance and saturation. Adjacent stack slices alternate luminance; same-luminance neighbors separate on the saturation axis. Navy-80 (특은채) is large-fills-only (≈2.2:1 vs --bg-surface): never lines, markers, or text.

rules.name: The Chart-Token-Only Rule
rules.body: Chart code obtains colors exclusively through semantic --chart-* tokens or their mirrors in src/lib/chart-colors.ts — never the raw --ms-* layer, never literal hex outside the token/mapping files.

dos: Do build hierarchy from background luminance steps (2–5%) and type weight — never from color.
Do keep semantic color (positive/negative/risk/info) to points: dots, badges, thin lines, emphasized digits.
Do render every number as tabular-nums, and every rate/price through PriceDisplay's 3-digit big-figure convention.
Do treat dark and light as two independently-tuned palettes serving two different desk activities.
Do keep the dockview panel header (Terminal Black, #0A0E14) dark in both modes; it's chrome, not content.
Do use only the 8px spacing scale (space-1 through space-8, skipping 5/7/9) and only rounded (4px) / rounded-md (6px).
Do use shadow-sm / shadow-md exclusively on popovers, modals, dropdowns, and dragged dockview panels — never on static cards.
donts: Don't add a gradient, thick border, or rounded-lg to a card to make it 'look designed'.
Don't use a colored panel background 'for visual interest' — color only appears where it carries meaning.

Don't use border-left/border-right as a colored accent stripe anywhere outside two sanctioned, functional exceptions: the sidebar's 2px active-nav-item bar, and the Backtest scenario card's 2px selected-state bar.
Don't render a number in a proportional font, or leave it non-tabular.
Don't use uppercase on a value or mixed-case on a category tag.
Don't use rounded-full anywhere except status dots and the user avatar.
Don't put emoji anywhere in the UI.
Don't conflate the KTB cash-curve tenor set (3Y/5Y/10Y/20Y/30Y) with the fuller IRS/CRS tenor set (3M–30Y).
Don't apply a gradient-text treatment (background-clip: text) anywhere.
